Gouge

rhymes with 'lounge' -- GOWJ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To gouge overcharge or make a hole.

Renters in the flooded neighborhood accused several landlords of trying to gouge desperate families searching for anywhere to live.

Worked Example

Right after the hurricane warning, one hardware store tripled the price of plywood and bottled water, clearly trying to gouge panicked customers who had nowhere else to shop.

Deliberately charging far more than something is worth, especially to people who have no other choice, is exactly what it means to gouge someone.

How Gouge Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

overcharge

overcharge: charge more than something is fairly worth

fleece

fleece: cheat someone out of money, often by overcharging

Antonyms

undercharge

undercharge: charge less than something is worth

discount

discount: reduce a price below the usual amount

How Strong Is It? — mark up → gouge → extort

mark up vs. gouge

mark up vs. gouge: Mark up is milder than gouge: a store marks up prices to make a fair profit, while to gouge customers is to overcharge them harshly and unfairly.

extort vs. gouge

extort vs. gouge: Extort is harsher than gouge: a company that gouges charges outrageously high prices, but extortion goes further, taking money through outright threats or abuse of power.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

root — gouge (Middle French gouge)

root — gouge (Middle French gouge): a curved chisel used to scoop out wood or stone; ultimately of Gaulish origin (Middle French, from Late Latin gubia)

Put it together

Put it together: Gouge started out as the name for a curved chisel used to scoop material out of wood or stone. Charging someone an unfair price is a figurative extension of that scooping motion -- the seller is effectively gouging an unfair amount of money out of the price.

Use the root in a new word: gouge (the tool)

Use the root in a new word: gouge (the tool): The woodworker used a curved gouge to carve a smooth channel into the tabletop.
